topic: EU AI Act obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models: requirements, systemic-risk models, code of practice and deadlines

key_points.point: GPAI provider obligations began applying on 2 August 2025: technical documentation, information for downstream providers, an EU copyright policy, and a public summary of training content.

atoms.fact: EU AI Act obligations for GPAI providers began applying on 2 August 2025.
GPAI providers must produce technical documentation.
GPAI providers must provide information for downstream providers.
GPAI providers must have an EU copyright policy.
GPAI providers must publish a public summary of training content.

key_points.point: A model trained with more than 10^25 FLOP is presumed to have high-impact capabilities and thus systemic risk; the Commission can also designate models and amend thresholds by delegated act.

atoms.fact: Under the EU AI Act, a GPAI model trained with more than 10^25 FLOP is presumed to have high-impact capabilities and thus systemic risk.
The Commission can also designate GPAI models as systemic-risk.
The Commission can amend the systemic-risk thresholds by delegated act.

key_points.point: Systemic-risk providers must additionally evaluate models (including adversarial testing), assess and mitigate systemic risks, report serious incidents to the AI Office, and ensure cybersecurity (Article 55).

atoms.fact: Under Article 55 of the EU AI Act, systemic-risk GPAI providers must additionally evaluate their models, including adversarial testing.
Systemic-risk GPAI providers must assess and mitigate systemic risks.
Systemic-risk GPAI providers must report serious incidents to the AI Office.
Systemic-risk GPAI providers must ensure cybersecurity.

key_points.point: Providers must notify the Commission without delay and within two weeks of meeting or foreseeing the 10^25 FLOP threshold, and may argue the model is not systemic-risk.

atoms.fact: GPAI providers must notify the Commission without delay and within two weeks of meeting or foreseeing the 10^25 FLOP threshold.
GPAI providers notifying the Commission about the 10^25 FLOP threshold may argue that their model is not systemic-risk.

key_points.point: Commission guidelines treat a model trained with more than about 10^23 FLOP that can generate language, text-to-image or text-to-video as indicatively general-purpose.

atoms.fact: Commission guidelines treat a model trained with more than about 10^23 FLOP that can generate language, text-to-image or text-to-video as indicatively general-purpose.

key_points.point: Free and open-source models are exempt from some documentation and EU-representative duties, but not from copyright policy and training-summary duties, and the exemption never applies to systemic-risk models.

atoms.fact: Free and open-source GPAI models are exempt from some documentation and EU-representative duties.
Free and open-source GPAI models are not exempt from the copyright policy and training-summary duties.
The exemption for free and open-source GPAI models never applies to systemic-risk models.

key_points.point: The GPAI Code of Practice, published 10 July 2025, has Transparency, Copyright and Safety and Security chapters; the last applies only to systemic-risk providers.

atoms.fact: The GPAI Code of Practice was published on 10 July 2025.
The GPAI Code of Practice has Transparency, Copyright and Safety and Security chapters.
The Safety and Security chapter of the GPAI Code of Practice applies only to systemic-risk providers.

key_points.point: The Commission and AI Board deemed the Code an adequate voluntary tool; signing brings reduced burden and more legal certainty, while non-signers must show compliance by other adequate means.

atoms.fact: The Commission and AI Board deemed the GPAI Code an adequate voluntary tool.
Signing the GPAI Code of Practice brings reduced burden and more legal certainty.
Non-signers of the GPAI Code of Practice must show compliance by other adequate means.

key_points.point: Most major providers signed the Code (including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and Amazon); xAI signed only the Safety and Security chapter.

atoms.fact: Most major providers signed the GPAI Code, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and Amazon.
xAI signed only the Safety and Security chapter of the GPAI Code of Practice.

key_points.point: The Commission's enforcement powers over GPAI providers, including fines of up to 3% of worldwide annual turnover or EUR 15 million (whichever is higher), have applied since 2 August 2026.

atoms.fact: The Commission's enforcement powers over GPAI providers have applied since 2 August 2026.
The Commission's enforcement powers over GPAI providers include fines of up to 3% of worldwide annual turnover or EUR 15 million, whichever is higher.

key_points.point: Models placed on the EU market before 2 August 2025 have until 2 August 2027 to comply.

atoms.fact: GPAI models placed on the EU market before 2 August 2025 have until 2 August 2027 to comply.

key_points.point: The Digital Omnibus on AI (in force 27 July 2026) postponed high-risk obligations (Annex III to 2 December 2027, Annex I to 2 August 2028) but did not postpone GPAI obligations.

atoms.fact: The EU Digital Omnibus on AI came into force on 27 July 2026.
The Digital Omnibus on AI postponed the AI Act's high-risk obligations for Annex III systems to 2 December 2027.
The Digital Omnibus on AI postponed the AI Act's high-risk obligations for Annex I systems to 2 August 2028.
The Digital Omnibus on AI did not postpone GPAI obligations.

key_points.point: On 14 October 2026 the AI Office sent its first formal requests for information to providers of GPAI models with systemic risk: the first use of its investigative powers.

atoms.fact: On 14 October 2026 the AI Office sent its first formal requests for information to providers of GPAI models with systemic risk.
The AI Office's first formal requests for information to providers of systemic-risk GPAI models were the first use of its investigative powers.
